AgentDefinitionMutationResponse.description:
The outcome of an agent-definition mutation. The full account of the
change — prior and new state under a named action — lives in the audit
trail.

AgentDefinitionScopeQuery.description: Scope filter for durable agent-definition reads and deletes.

ApprovalDecisionScope.description: How widely an approved decision should apply.

ApprovalDecisionValue.description: The human verdict on a pending approval.

AssemblyHistoryEntry.description: One turn whose persisted assembly report can be opened in the context inspector.

AuditEventCursor.description:
Where a page of the audit record ended, handed back for the next request
as `before` and `before_id`.

AuditEventListResponse.description:
A page of the audit record, newest first, under the filters the request
named. `next_cursor` names the page after this one — absent when this
page ends the record.

AuditEventView.description: One event of the local audit record, as recorded.

ConfigurationHistoryEvent.description: One durable configuration change as recorded at the mutation boundary.

CreateAgentDefinitionRequest.description: Whole definition supplied when creating a durable agent.

DeliveryRoutingRequest.description:
Where output should be routed once a run completes.

`deliver_to_origin` defaults to true for channel-initiated turns, where
an origin always exists. Callers without an origin (schedules, manual
API calls) must set it false or target resolution errors.

DeliveryTarget.description: A destination for a run's output.

DeviceResponse.description:
A registered device as the gateway lists it. `capabilities` are what the
device last advertised on connecting; empty until it first dials in.

EffectiveAgentDefinitionResponse.description: An agent definition available when creating a session in one topic.

selectable.description:
Whether the picker offers it for a new session; a platform agent that
runs only where the platform runs it is listed but not offered.

EffectiveAgentDefinitionSourceScope.description: Where an effective agent definition comes from.

ExternalChannelIntegration.description: An external channel integration that can receive delivered output.

GateConfig.description:
A cheap-model check that runs before the main model wakes.

The gate model inspects the schedule's message, the optional criteria,
and the previous run's outcome, then verdicts `run` or `skip`. Its
decision and reasoning are recorded on the run.

criteria.description:
What "work needed" means for this schedule. When absent the gate
judges from the schedule message and previous outcome alone.

model.description: Model id or alias from the configured model catalogue.

observations.description:
State the gate is shown before it decides, beyond the schedule's own
record: what the criteria name. Declared here so a criterion about a
file is decidable against that file, and refused at declaration when
the schedule's session has nowhere to read it from.

GateObservation.description: One thing a gate observes before deciding.

oneOf.description:
A file under the scheduled session's trusted workspace, by a path
relative to it: the gate sees whether it exists, its size, and its
opening excerpt.

GateWarning.description:
A flag raised when a gate is declared: something about the declaration
the operator should know before the first fire. Derived from the gate as
stored, never persisted, so every surface that shows the schedule shows
the same flags.

oneOf.description:
Criteria were declared but nothing is observed, so a criterion about
a file or other workspace state can never be decided against that
state: the gate skips such a criterion and names what it did not
observe, rather than guessing at every fire.

GitCredentialRequest.description: One HTTPS git credential lookup on the turn's private IPC socket.

directory.description:
The directory git ran the helper in: the repository asking, which
decides the operator's directory-conditional configuration.

GitCredentialResponse.description: An absent credential makes git continue without this helper's answer.

GitSignRequest.description:
One request to sign a git payload on the host, from the sandboxed git's
signing program over the turn's private IPC socket, in the operator's
signing format. The payload is base64-encoded.

oneOf.description:
`ssh-keygen -Y sign`: the signing namespace git names (`git`) and the
public key git was configured with.

GitSignResponse.description:
The armoured signature for the payload, or the refusal that explains why
the host did not sign. An OpenPGP signature comes with the signer's
status lines, which git reads to confirm the signature was made.

KnowledgeMirrorRegenerateResponse.description:
Result of regenerating a topic's knowledge-base browse mirror — a
disposable markdown projection of the database-authoritative store.

mirror_root.description: Absolute path of the regenerated mirror directory.

OperatorHistoryResponse.description: Read-only history reconstructed from the local audit and context records.

OperatorSessionEnding.description: A terminal turn's standing on the operator surface.

awaiting_approval.description: The running turn is held on a request only the person can answer.

source.description: The schedule or workflow run that opened this session, when applicable.

topic_id.description: Absent for a session in the general scope.

topic_name.description: The topic's name, or "General" for a session without one.

SandboxPolicy.description:
Per-turn sandbox policy and timeouts.

Serialised to the sandboxed child, which applies the write set and the
broad read through Landlock; the host applies the same policy through
bubblewrap's mounts, where the masks and the read-only paths are enforced.

environment.description: Host-selected environment inherited by sandboxed commands.

host_network.description:
Whether sandboxed commands share the host's network. Without it the
sandbox has its own network namespace, reaching the network only
through an egress proxy when the host binds one in.

masked_paths.description:
Private paths hidden from the sandbox altogether. A directory reads as
empty; a file reads as empty. Enforced by the mount layer, so the
fallback backend cannot honour them.

read_only_paths.description:
Paths kept read-only even where a write path above them would allow
writing: a read-only attachment inside a writable tree, say.

shutdown_grace_period.description: Time to wait for graceful shutdown before SIGKILL.

tool_output_directory.description:
Where tools keep their output artefacts, carried to the child
independently of its working directory; writable, as a write path.

tool_runtime.description:
Session tool settings carried to the child, which builds its tools
from them.

working_directory.description:
The directory the agent's commands run in. Writable only when it is
also in `write_paths`.

write_paths.description:
Paths the sandboxed process may write. Everything else it can see is
read-only.

Schedule.description: A schedule as returned by the API.

creator.description: Where this schedule came from — a person or an agent.

gate_warnings.description:
Declaration-time flags on the gate, derived from it as stored; empty
when there is no gate or nothing to flag.

ScheduleCreator.description:
Who created a schedule.

This is provenance, not a request field: the surface that creates the
schedule stamps it (the settings UI and HTTP surface stamp `user`; the
scheduling tools stamp `agent`), so an agent cannot claim a schedule was
a person's. It answers the audit question "where did this schedule come
from" wherever schedules are listed.

oneOf.description: A person, through the settings automation panel or the HTTP surface.

An agent, through the scheduling tools. Carries the id of the agent
that made it.

ScheduleSpec.description:
When a schedule fires.

- `one_shot` — a single RFC 3339 instant.
- `interval` — natural-language `"every N seconds|minutes|hours|days"`.
- `cron` — a cron expression (seconds-resolution, as parsed by the
  `cron` crate).

ScheduleStatus.description: Lifecycle status of a schedule definition.

oneOf.description:
A one-shot that has fired, or an interval/cron with no next
occurrence.

SessionPolicy.description:
Which session each run executes in.

- `fresh` — every run creates a new session in the selected topic, or
  the general scope when `topic_id` is absent, for
  `agent_id`, with a deliberately assembled opening context (the
  schedule's message plus the previous run's outcome).
- `continuation` — every run continues the named session, executing as
  whatever agent that session has at run time.

UpdateAgentDefinitionRequest.description: Whole replacement supplied when updating a durable agent definition.

VariantSelectionHistoryEvent.description: One recorded experiment selection, exposed only in operator history.
